_meta.title: wiki-sourced intrinsic in-game stat caps (#199, #661)
_meta.note: A stat whose in-game value stops counting past a fixed ceiling. Applied as a SECOND source of truth into the solver's cappedStats, beside the player's own per-stat caps; the tighter of the two wins, per the Stat cap clause in CONCEPTS.md. This said THIRD until #661, counting an armor dodge cap that #573 deleted — there is no longer a category-keyed armor clamp, and Dodge is disclosed rather than clamped.
_meta.evidence_rule: Every entry carries the verbatim wiki sentence stating the ceiling, and the page it was read from. A stat whose ceiling the wiki does not state outright gets NO entry — see `refused` below, which exists so the same four stats are not re-guessed.
_meta.why_refusals_are_recorded: Four of the five stats harvested for #199 have no ceiling, and three of those four look like they should. Doubleshot in particular is Doublestrike's documented sibling and behaves in the OPPOSITE way past 100%. Recording only the confirmation would leave the next reader to re-derive the refusals, and the cheap wrong answer is one analogy away.
_meta.sweeps: Two, both in the evidence file. 2026-08-28 (#199) harvested Doublestrike, Doubleshot, Fortification, Dodge, Concealment. 2026-09-01 harvested Strikethrough, off-hand strike chance, Jump, Incorporeal, secondary shield bash chance; only Strikethrough is recorded here so far. Off-hand strike chance is confirmed at 100 and deliberately NOT recorded (the Two Weapon Fighting non-goal, same reasoning as the Doublestrike note); Jump is confirmed at 40 and is a disclosure question rather than a cap (#663); the two refusals are #662.

caps.quote: Doublestrike above 100% has no effect on main-hand weapons.
caps.note: Main-hand reading only. The same page states a separate off-hand ceiling (50%, 65% with Perfect Two Weapon Fighting) which is deliberately NOT modelled: keying a cap on wielding two weapons is the Two Weapon Fighting penalty, an AGENTS.md non-goal that is disclosed to the player rather than modelled numerically.

caps.quote: If your Strikethrough Chance is 400% or higher, you will always attack a fifth target (if in range). Strikethrough effectively caps at 400%, in that while higher values are possible, they do not provide chances to attack sixth or further targets.
caps.note: NOT a clamp. The page says higher values 'are possible' and the game does not truncate them — what stops at 400 is the BENEFIT, which is this table's semantics ('value above this buys nothing') and the same reading as Doublestrike. Do not restate it as a hard ceiling: the tiers below it (over 100% guarantees a second target, 200% a third, 300% a fourth, 400% a fifth) are why 400 is the number, and there is no sixth target to buy. Unlike Doublestrike this ceiling is genuinely reachable: gear alone tops out at 15 (Artifact bucket only), but the feat and enhancement lines clear 400 in combination — base 20, Two Handed Fighting +60, Improved/Greater/Perfect +30 each, Two Handed Specialty +120, Dance of Death +50/100/200 — so it binds through declared credits on real two-handed builds.

refused.reason: No ceiling — it wraps past 100% into extra shots.
refused.quote: If your Doubleshot is greater than 100%, then a second shot is guaranteed, and the remainder is the chance at additional shots.
refused.note: Do NOT add this by analogy with Doublestrike. The two are named as siblings on each other's pages, described in parallel language, and behave in opposite ways past 100%. Capping it deletes every point a ranged build earned above 100.

refused.reason: No ceiling — 300% is a normal target for a durable build, because bosses bypass a portion.
refused.quote: In DDO, most players strive for roughly +10% fortification per level, with the most durable characters achieving +300% at level 30.

refused.reason: The cap is player-built, not a constant: Maximum Dodge Bonus BEGINS at 25% and an entire section of the page lists ways to raise it. The one true constant (a 95% hard cap) is unreachable from gear.
refused.quote: The Maximum Dodge Bonus begins at 25%. This Maximum Dodge Bonus amount can be increased through various means (see Increasing Maximum Dodge).
refused.note: The armor-type reduction is modelled separately and approximately by ARMOR_DODGE_CAP in web/model.js; that constant's own unsourced numbers are #573.

refused.reason: No numeric cap stated. The page rules on stacking (highest of a type applies), which the solver's max-within-bucket semantics already reproduce.
refused.quote: Generally, multiple concealment bonuses of the same type do not stack, whether beneficial or offensive in nature, only the greatest concealment number applies.
refused.note: Checked because #140's U5 made Concealment a credited stat for the first time.
